contexts.finding: PF sample selectivity can reappear between distractors, while match enhancement and repetition suppression have different task dependence. These observations do not establish a causal local storage or PF-to-IT route.
limitations: Two rhesus monkeys supplied 264 screened PF units; 145 task-responsive units were retained (98 in the ABBA-trained animal and 47 in the standard-task animal). The other 109 units were not studied further. Cells are nested within two animals; this is not an unbiased PF prevalence estimate. Sex and ages are unspecified.

The sample and test images last 500 ms with 1000-ms blank intervals and zero to four intervening nonmatches. ABBA trials repeat an irrelevant nonmatch; standard trials do not. Task/training differences are confounded with animal identity. PF visual responses use 90-290 ms after onset and delay activity the last 600 ms of each blank interval.

The text reports forty delay-selective units, including 33/98 ABBA and 7/47 standard units; Table 1 instead lists 32/98 for ABBA. Match-enhancement counts also differ across the text and table, with mixed response types. No exact reconciled subgroup prevalence or exclusive partition is admitted.

The 135 IT units were previously recorded in the ABBA animal and reanalyzed. They are not simultaneous paired PF-IT recordings or an independent replication. Figure 7 pools forty PF units across two animals against twenty-five IT units from one animal; selection and animal composition differ.

Best/worst-sample traces use selected neurons and sample rankings. Reported half-trial discriminant classification excludes the first delay and averages 20.8% versus six-way chance of 16.7%; the paper does not specify that unit selection was nested within training folds. No classification, multiplicity correction or neural minimum is independently reproduced.

PF feedback to IT is proposed in the Discussion. The authors explicitly state that the direct PF-deactivation test of IT match enhancement had not been tried. Response precedence, delay persistence and ramping do not identify an exclusive local recurrence, directed feedback route, accumulator or complete control circuit.

contexts.finding: Post-pulse unattended-category evidence exceeds chance after cue 1 but not after cue 2.
limitations: Category classifiers distinguish face, word and motion information. Above-chance category evidence does not demonstrate recovery of the particular remembered item. Below-chance-threshold evidence is not absence of all neuronal activity; fMRI and EEG are different readouts.

The supplementary protocol gives different initial delays across experiments (7, 5 and 2 seconds), whereas Figure 1 supplies a generic timeline. TMS timing is measured after cue offset: 2.5 seconds in Experiments 2 and 4, and 2-3 seconds with jitter in Experiment 3. One schematic is not a common exact trial manifest.

EEG features undergo 2.5-second centered temporal smoothing. This mixes past and future samples and does not establish precise millisecond reactivation latency. All-trial normalization and trial-level cross-validation do not provide a held-out-person generalization estimate. The stated 191 training trials fits Experiment 3 but does not transparently describe the 164-trial Experiment 2 sessions.

TMS occurs on every EEG trial. State/category comparisons do not substitute for sham or no-TMS trials within the same EEG preparation. Modeled cortical fields, scalp targets and source-inversion meshes are not measured synaptic connections. Neither synaptic weights nor an exclusive silent storage carrier was directly measured.

Main text, all four main figures, the complete supplementary scientific text, all six supplementary figures and Table S1 were reviewed. Raw trials, participant allocation records, custom code and Movie S1 were not reproduced. Inconsistent figure cross-references are resolved only to visibly identified panels, not by inventing missing results.

The right-precuneus target derives from the motion localizer. Cue 2 differs in relevance, elapsed trial phase and prior pulse exposure; separate significance tests are not a fully isolated causal relevance interaction. A null decoder does not demonstrate erasure of every possible representation.
